reviews.review:
QUICK REVIEW - game requires very little skill, and very much luck for RNG (that's it, that's the review) 

This is one of those many times that I wish Steam had a "meh" option for a review. But if I have to lean either yes or no, I think I'm going to lean "No", despite the hours played. 

[b][u]Issue #1 - The Roguelite Grind[/u][/b]
I have a strong issue with Roguelites. My issue is that most of the time, the game just forces you through a grind that isn't necessary. You have to start a run, die, get points, spend points, go on a run again, repeat. That's not good game play, that's a "beat your hand against the wall" game loop. Thankfully, 99% of your "skill tree" goes across all the available characters. There's about 5 skills you have to buy that is unique to each character.

A much smarter approach to this would be just limiting the upgrades you can get in game to the difficulty you've selected. As you increase difficulty, you're allowed to get more and more in game upgrades, but you HAVE to finish the previous difficulty before unlocking the next one. This "trains" the player and prevents them from jumping into a harder difficulty and ruining the fun for everyone else because they think they're God's greatest gift to humanity. 

Thankfully, the initial grind isn't TOO long, but I wanted to put that out there anyway. 

[b][u]Issue #2 - Damage Sponges[/u][/b]
As you increase the difficulty, you give the enemies more and more and more and more and more health. You also add more and more traps through the stages. The traps are extremely annoying, but I'll talk about that in the next issue. 

Damage sponges are just NOT fun. It's just NOT. I wish developers would get that through their heads. There is nothing fun about unloading 200+ rounds into a regular enemy's head. It's silly. If you want a challenge that's actually fun, add more enemies, make them more deadly, and decrease their health. Simple. 

#nomoredamagesponges

[b][u]Issue #3 - Audio[/u][/b]
The audio is terribad. There is almost zero audio cues for the player to determine how/where they're taking damage. Those traps I mentioned in the last part? Yeah, you about can't tell when you're standing in one. Me and my brother have played all the way through Reincarnation 8, and the phrase we said the most was "why am I taking damage" and "what's hurting me?". Honest to goodness, more often than not we were standing next to fire blasting out of a trap or something and we just COULD NOT tell because of the lack of audio cues. It's crazy. 

And on the topic of audio, for the love of all that is holy, WHY is all the sound and music 100x louder in the Abyssal Serpent fight? Every. Single. Time. 

[b][u]Issue #4 - The Roguelite Dice Roll[/u][/b]
This is another big issue I have with roguelites because most of them are made poorly. There's a big dependency on good RNG when it comes to your survival. This means a few bad rolls at the beginning will entirely shutdown your entire run. This often led to either me or my brother often doing 2-3x the damage of the other player and having to carry the other. On the other hand, sometimes you'll get all the good rolls and a boss can't even kill you on Reincarnation 6 because you have so much health regen going on. 

I acknowledge the fact that it's harder to balance a game when things get randomized, but if you can't do it, then you don't need to do it. I don't want the success of my run almost entirely dependent on RNG. I want it to depend on my skill. 

[b][u]Other Notes and Tidbits[/u][/b]
The game IS fun to play. The controls are nice (when they work). The guns are all unique and fun, though some are just downright incredibly useless, they are least neat. The characters are awesome. They look super cool and all bring their own skills to the table, some which work and some I wonder if the devs even tried. 

I enjoy how each zone/world is one big map, but it picks sections of that map at random and you go through it different ways. I find that more enjoyable than just completely randomized levels. It's interesting to get used to a certain room only to be thrown for a loop when you approach that same room on another run, but backwards. 

The bosses...well, the original 3 bosses are cool. They're fine. The three bosses they added as "alternatives" in the same stages are horrendous, with Stage 2 just leaving me scratching my head and asking myself "what in the world were they thinking"? 

[b][u]The Results[/u][/b]
And this is why I want to give it a "meh". Because there are neat and fun parts, but there's also a bunch of issues holding all the good things back. But, since I have to choose either Yes or No, I'm going with "No". I'll probably still give it some more hours cause it's a good way to spend time with the brother, and there's a couple cheese builds I want to try, but as a "quality product", no.

If you like borderlands or any kind of looter shooter, and also want a roguelike influence this is a fantastic game. it is incredibly simple over all even with all the different weapons, characters, scrolls, but it has insane depth when it comes to really maxing the ♥♥♥♥ out of your character for each run. Each character emphasizes different styles of play that are all totally viable and insanely fun, plus you have a talent tree that will max out at level 168 right now this game can give you alot of enjoyment and play time. I highly recommend this game for anyone who wants a challenge or just really enjoys shooting and seeing the numbers go up.
